To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DFT calculations of the 1H and 13C NMR spectra of 1-butyl-pyridinium halide salts can provide reliable predictions of the chemical shifts of the ionic liquid in bulk solution and that the DFT results are not significantly affected by dynamic effects due to temperature and vibrational motion.

the simple DFT approach is capable of providing a good description of the NMR features of 1-butyl-pyridinium halide ILs, provided that the bulk structure of these ILs is dominated, in solution, by H-bonding interactions.

i) the ionic liquid 1-butylpyridinium chloride is dominated by H bonds between the chloride anion and the pyridine ortho protons; ii) DFT calculations of selected supramolecular arrangements of the ionic liquid provide a very good agreement with the experimental NMR spectra; iii) dynamic effects due to temperature, and conformational and vibrational motions are not very significant for the chloride salt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the bulk structure of ionic liquids based upon 1-butylpyridinium halides and bromide salts.
the study of the ion-pairing structure in 1-but-3-methyl-3-pyridinium halide and tribromide ionic liquids, using a combination of experimental and DFT based approaches.

the development of a DFT based protocol for the characterization of the bulk structure of ionic liquids, and it is also aimed at testing whether a simple DTF based approach is capable to describe the structure of ionic liquid in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DFT based calculations can be successfully applied to the prediction of NMR chemical shifts in ionic liquids.
the DFT calculations can provide a reliable description of the NMR properties of ILs, but the results should be interpreted with caution, especially when the H-bonds are weak.
DFT based calculations of the NMR chemical shifts in ionic liquids, although not yet fully reliable, are very promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DFT calculations of selected supramolecular aggregates are capable of providing reliable predictions of the experimental NMR spectra of ionic liquids, but only if the bulk structure is dominated by H bonding.

a DFT based protocol can be applied to predict NMR chemical shifts for the ionic liquids based 1-butyl-pyridinium halides, but the reliability of the method is limited by the structural features of the IL.

, for the 1-butyl-picolinium halides, the simple DFT based calculations are able to provide reliable predictions of the NMR chemical shifts and that the ion-pairing arrangement can be predicted with a good degree of confidence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple DFT calculation can provide an excellent description of the NMR chemical shifts in ionic liquids, and that the protocol can be applied to a wide range of systems, even in the presence of multiple ion-pairing arrangements.
, in general, the simple DFT based protocol is able to provide an adequate description of the NMR chemical shifts for the ionic liquids under study.
, when the H- bond is strong and the ion pairing is not too weak, DFT can be used as a reliable and fast tool to predict the NMR spectra.
